items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship in beta for pull request review
items.summary: Claude Ship is available today in beta and combines the generally available Code Review feature with two new agents in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. It can review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones a team's policy allows, with a new /ship command in Claude Code.

evidence.quote: Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team's policy allows.
That's why we built Claude Ship , available today in beta.
It can review PRs, fix them, and decide what's ready to merge based on policies each team sets.
How Claude Ship works: review, fix, and approve Claude Ship is made up of Code Review , which is already generally available, and two new agents in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals.
Code Review gives teams fast reviews, clear findings, and a choice of Quick, Standard, or Deep review levels for each repository.
Two ways to get started For developers: /ship it from Claude Code Developers can try Claude Ship on their own pull requests with the new /ship command in Claude Code.
Admins choose the review level (Quick, Standard, or Deep), choose when reviews run, and configure spend limits.
Code Review is generally available , and PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta.

items.title: OpenAI and Cisco open-source Shirudo for Linux runtime protection
items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco are launching Shirudo, an open-source runtime that helps teams protect Linux systems while they roll out patches. It uses eBPF to block vulnerable code paths without restarting the system, and in a controlled test a Codex-generated shield stopped a Java4Shell exploit attempt against a running Elasticsearch service.

evidence.quote: Rethinking infrastructure Building in the open OpenAI and Cisco are launching Shirudo, an open-source runtime that helps teams protect Linux systems while they roll out patches.
In a controlled test ⁠ (opens in a new window) , a Codex-generated shield blocked a Java4Shell exploit attempt against a running Elasticsearch service without requiring a restart.
” Greg Brockman, President and Co-founder of OpenAI How Shirudo works Shirudo uses eBPF, a Linux technology that allows small programs to run at specific points inside the operating system.
OpenAI and Cisco are designing Shirudo around four core capabilities: Live protection: eBPF shields can block vulnerable code paths without restarting the system.
Trusted deployment: Shields are cryptographically signed and verified before loading.
Using OpenAI's Codex, the team generated a shield that added an input check to Java's Base64 decoder and attached it directly to a running Elasticsearch process.
When attempting to exploit the vulnerability, the shield rejected the malicious input, blocking the attack while Elasticsearch continued running.

Building in the open OpenAI and Cisco are open-sourcing Shirudo ⁠ (opens in a new window) so developers, security researchers, and infrastructure operators can inspect the code, test protections, and contribute to its development.
Shirudo is licensed under BSD 2-Clause, with its BPF programs dual-licensed under BSD and GPL.

items.title: Google DeepMind uses Gemini 4 agents and Lean to speed up quantum algorithms
items.summary: Teams of Gemini 4 agents improved well-known quantum algorithms for fusion and chemistry, producing highly efficient quantum circuits. The agent teams proved each result with Lean and cut the required computing cost by 11.8×, while lowering required memory from 5,650 to 4,338 error-corrected qubits; the Lean library, problem specifications, and verified solutions are open-sourced.

evidence.quote: In a new paper , we used teams of Gemini 4 agents to improve well-known quantum algorithms, creating highly efficient quantum circuits.
To help the community build on this work, we are open-sourcing our Lean library , problem specifications, and verified solutions on GitHub.
Our agent teams proved each result using Lean, a formal theorem prover.
Our agent teams cut the required computing cost (a metric that combines required qubits and operations) by 11.8×, and lowered required memory from 5,650 to 4,338 error-corrected qubits .
We built a new, open-source library , in Lean for quantum algorithms which could be used by teams of collaborating agents, so their ideas were backed by mathematical correctness guarantees.

items.title: inclusionAI releases Ling-3.2-air as an open-weight model
items.summary: Ling-3.2-air is an open-weight model sharing the same native multimodal architecture as Ling-3.0-flash-VL, with a total parameter scale of 124B and 5.5B activated. Its AutomationBench-AA score rises from 15.7% to 61%, and its pass rate on Terminal-Bench 4.0 rises from 0% to 27%.

evidence.quote: We introduce Ling-3.2-air , an open-weight model that shares the same native multimodal architecture as Ling-3.0-flash-VL .
Its AutomationBench-AA score rises from 15.7% to 61% , while its GDP.pdf all-pass rate increases from 8.4% to 16% .
On AA-Briefcase v1.1 , its Elo rating rises from 987 to 1340 , a gain of 353 points .
On Terminal-Bench 4.0 , its pass rate on terminal-based tasks rises from 0% to 27% .
Parameter Scale Total 124B, Activated 5.5B

items.title: Google Research proposes DeepCrossAttention for transformer residual connections
items.summary: DeepCrossAttention (DCA) generalizes residual connections with learnable weights and depth-wise cross-attention, letting each layer dynamically select and route outputs from previous layers. The ICML 2025 work reports comparable or improved learning while reducing parameters by up to 30-40%, and DCA adds less than 0.2% of the total model size.

evidence.quote: We present DeepCrossAttention (DCA), an architecture that enhances transformer networks by using learnable weights and depth-wise cross-attention to dynamically combine outputs from previous layers, preventing the information dilution seen in traditional residual connections.

In our ICML 2025 paper, "DeepCrossAttention: Supercharging Transformer Residual Connections ," we studied the shortcomings of the traditional residual architecture and introduced DeepCrossAttention (DCA), which generalizes residual connections by allowing each layer to dynamically select and route f

By allowing the model to dynamically choose which previous layers are most important at any given moment, DCA achieves comparable or improved learning, while reducing the number of parameters needed by up to 30-40%.

To achieve a perplexity of <14 on LM1B, a standard transformer with fixed width required 42 layers, whereas the DCA model achieved a lower perplexity with only 30 layers — a 29% reduction in depth and parameter count.

DCA adds a tiny number of parameters — less than 0.2% of the total model size — making it negligible in terms of compute and memory footprint, while increasing memory bandwidth, as representations from different layers are presented intact rather than blended together.

Interestingly, because DCA can be initialized to behave identically to a standard residual network, it doesn’t require training from scratch: retrofitting DCA onto an already pre-trained transformer and briefly continuing training reduced perplexity by 0.19 on LM1B, compared to just 0.02 for continu

items.title: Duopra learns full-duplex conversation and task execution together
items.summary: Duopra is a full-duplex interaction model that treats the backend as a tool and learns task execution alongside conversational control through protocol SFT, full-duplex RL, and projector-only repair. On Full-Duplex-Bench v3 it reaches 47.7% Pass@1 with direct tool execution and 49.3% with a DeepSeek backend.

items.title: cmHC balances stream mixing in manifold-constrained hyper-connections
items.summary: cmHC is an exact doubly stochastic method that geometrically contracts the Birkhoff polytope toward its interior, mitigating under-mixing in hyper-connections without new parameterization. The authors also develop fused operators for cmHC on Ascend NPUs, reducing hyper-connection execution latency by up to 44.8%.

evidence.quote: Generated by deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) extends residual connections to multiple streams and stabilizes residual propagation by constraining stream-mixing residual matrices to the Birkhoff polytope , the set of doubly stochastic matrices .

We reveal a mixing trade-off: when under-mixed residual matrices stay close to the vertices of the Birkhoff polytope , hyper-connections will degenerate into a set of nearly independent streams; when over-mixed residual matrices are concentrated around the uniform barycenter of the polytope, streams

Motivated by these findings, we propose Contraction for Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections ( cmHC ), an exact doubly stochastic method which geometrically contracts the Birkhoff polytope toward its interior.
This contraction mitigates under-mixing by forcing the residual matrices to explore deeper into the polytope, with a provable stream mixing bound and no new parameterization .
We also develop fused operators for cmHC on Ascend NPUs , reducing hyper-connection execution latency by up to 44.8%.

items.title: NoPeWorld prevents object penetration in interactive video world models
items.summary: The authors introduce NoPeBench to test how world models respond to physical obstacles and NoPeWorld, a lightweight framework that trains a small prediction head on a frozen DiT's hidden states to detect unsafe actions. NoPeWorld reduces the physical violation rate, averaged over six video world models, from 74% to 16%.

evidence.quote: To understand how existing models handle this, we introduce NoPeBench , a benchmark that evaluates how world models respond to physical obstacles.
We find that the hidden states of diffusion transformers (DiTs) can predict whether a candidate action will penetrate an obstacle.
Building on this, we introduce NoPeWorld , a lightweight framework that detects and prevents penetration.
Specifically, we train a small prediction head on top of a frozen DiT 's hidden states to read out if a candidate action is safe or not.
Unsafe actions are then replaced with safe ones that best preserve the original intent.
Despite its simplicity, NoPeWorld substantially reduces the physical violation rate , averaged over six video world models, from 74% to 16%.
Remarkably, our method shows zero-shot generalization to open-domain imagery, third-person viewpoints, and moving obstacles.

items.title: Future-OPSD learns video foresight reasoning without annotations
items.summary: Future-OPSD is an on-policy self-distillation framework that turns past-future video pairs into a self-supervised signal without extra annotations or LLM supervision, using a foresight score to emphasize decision-relevant content. On open-ended prediction and closed-ended planning, it improves base models by up to 14.2 and 15.9 points.

evidence.quote: We address this with an on-policy self-distillation framework that turns past-future video pairs into a natural self-supervised signal without extra annotations or LLM supervision .
We address this by defining a foresight score , from which we obtain a contrastive privilege advantage that drives the model to learn the most valuable future information.
We call the resulting framework Future-OPSD .
On open-ended prediction and closed-ended planning , Future-OPSD improves base models by up to 14.2 and 15.9 points without compromising general video understanding .

items.title: Reasoning Transfer via Captioning improves text-aware super-resolution
items.summary: The authors evaluate twelve recent super-resolution models and find a consistent, substantial performance drop on reasoning-required text, and propose RTC, a training-free plug-in that uses an external MLLM to infer degraded text for a text-conditioned SR model. RTC consistently improves all six text-conditioned SR models evaluated.

items.title: ReSpaceBench benchmarks persistent spatial memory across revisits
items.summary: ReSpaceBench contains 3,244 questions across 590 synthetic and real-home scenes, organized into 9 tasks covering room association, persistent state tracking, and downstream reasoning. Across 32 models and 3 agentic video-understanding frameworks, the strongest evaluated zero-shot model achieves 50.5% overall accuracy versus 90.1% for human annotators.

items.title: RoboTrack releases a robotic manipulation point-tracking benchmark and models
items.summary: RoboTrack introduces a benchmark, a synthetic training dataset, and two point tracking models for real-world robotic manipulation. RoboTrack-Bench contains 307 human-annotated videos with 2,522 point tracks, the synthetic training dataset is RoboTrack-15M, and the released models are RoboTracker and RoboTracker-Warp.

evidence.quote: RoboTrack-Bench contains 307 human-annotated videos from DROID, Ego-Exo4D, MolmoAct 2 , and EgoVerse, covering different robots and human hands, cluttered scenes, and first- and third-person viewpoints.
This pipeline produces RoboTrack-15M , a new synthetic training dataset targeted toward robotic manipulation.
Today, we’re releasing both RoboTrack components and two new point tracking models: RoboTracker and RoboTracker-Warp .

Both models improve average AJ across the three robotics benchmarks compared with their respective released baselines, and RoboTracker-Warp achieves state-of-the-art performance on four out of the five benchmarks we evaluated.
It contains 307 videos from DROID, Ego-Exo4D, MolmoAct 2, and EgoVerse, annotated with a total of 2,522 point tracks.
Their score drops by 3.0 to 6.6 AJ.
Even the strongest off-the-shelf tracker, CoWTracker, drops from 70.5 AJ on RoboTAP to 63.9 on RoboTrack-Bench.

items.title: Hugging Face outlines eight steps for building an agentic evaluation
items.summary: The post walks through eight steps for building and maintaining a useful agentic evaluation, from defining the claim and finding a task to reporting scores and comparing models. It notes that in an audit of Terminal-Bench, holding the model fixed and changing the agent harness moved accuracy by up to 29.9 percentage points.

evidence.quote: AI evaluations help shape which systems people build, adopt, and trust.
Building and maintaining a useful evaluation therefore takes real work: defining tasks that reflect domain expertise, scoring them reliably, and checking that the results support the claims made.
For instance, in an audit of Terminal-Bench , researchers kept the model fixed and changed the agent harness.
Accuracy varied by up to 29.9 percentage points.
We work through eight steps: define the claim , find a task , run it unchanged , adapt it , check the evaluation , read the traces , report the score , and compare models .

items.title: Anthropic opens Enterprise Frontier Safeguards public beta
items.summary: Anthropic is opening Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) in public beta, providing automated safety monitoring that analyzes data stored entirely on infrastructure controlled by customers. The setup keeps zero data retention (ZDR), with neither Anthropic nor cloud providers retaining enterprise data, and inputs and outputs are never used for model or classifier training.

evidence.quote: EFS provides state-of-the-art detection of sophisticated misuse, while remaining compatible with zero data retention (ZDR): neither Anthropic nor any cloud providers retain enterprises' data.
Enterprise Frontier Safeguards delivers just that.” Noopur Davis, EVP, Chief Information Security and Product Privacy Officer 1 / 5 Now, we're opening up EFS in public beta.
To catch attacks like these, we use a second defensive layer, known as automated safety monitoring.
This layer looks for patterns of misuse across many requests.
Through EFS, Anthropic can provide automated safety monitoring without storing any customer data.
Instead, our automated safety monitoring system analyzes data stored entirely on infrastructure controlled by our customers.
These cases can be read from your cloud storage or through an API, and can be integrated with security information and event management systems.
This provides you the following guarantees: Zero data retention .
Neither Anthropic nor your cloud provider retains your data.
You configure your own access policies and audit logging, and encrypt safety data with your own keys.
We never train on your data.
Inputs and outputs are used only for automated safety monitoring, never for model or classifier training.

items.title: obra/superpowers ships an agentic skills framework for coding agents
items.summary: Superpowers is a software development methodology for coding agents built on composable skills and initial instructions that ensure the agent applies them. It covers the flow from design sign-off and implementation planning to subagent-driven development, with agents working through each engineering task and reviewing their work; it is available via the official Claude plugin marketplace and the official Codex plugin marketplace.

evidence.quote: superpowers Public Sponsor Notifications You must be signed in to change notification settings Fork 28.8k ( 28.8k ) Star 325k ( 325k ) You must be signed in to star a repository About An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.
Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.
It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent.

After you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow.
Next up, once you say "go", it launches a subagent-driven-development process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward.
And because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special.
Superpowers is available via the official Claude plugin marketplace
